name: FocusRing
purpose: Provide one consistent keyboard-focus indicator shared by every interactive component.
intent: Centralize :focus-visible styling so no component defines its own one-off focus treatment.
useCases: Wrapping a custom-built interactive element that needs a focus indicator
Composing focus styling onto an element that already has its own classes (e.g. a raw input inside a custom control)
antiPatterns: Standalone decoration with no real focusable element
A one-off :focus-visible rule written locally instead of reusing this primitive

anatomy.element: React.ReactElement (via FocusRing) or any element (via focusRingClassNames)
anatomy.description: The single focusable element the focus classes are applied to. FocusRing has no DOM node of its own - it clones its child.

children.description: The single focusable element to clone and merge focus classes onto.

borderWidth.description: Outline width. Figma's focus-ring component currently has only one width (2px) - the prop is kept for forward compatibility if a denser variant is introduced later.

disabled.description: Suppresses the outline entirely - use only when the wrapped control is itself disabled.

className.description: Composes with the merged class list.

default.purpose: Standard outline width for all controls.

slots.name: children
supports: a single native or custom focusable element

offset.note: Not yet backed by a dedicated token - see Future Enhancements.

requirements: Only ever appears on :focus-visible, never on plain mouse :hover or :focus.
Does not make a non-focusable element focusable - the child must already be a real focusable element.
Does not add ARIA roles or labels - the wrapped element remains responsible for its own accessible name/role/value.

keyboardInteraction: Appears automatically whenever the wrapped element receives keyboard focus (:focus-visible).
behaviorRules: Clone the single child element and merge the focus classes onto its className.
disabled=true suppresses the outline via focusRingClassNames.focusRingDisabled instead of the width-specific class.
border-radius: inherit, so the ring shape always matches whatever element it wraps.
compositionRules: Every interactive atom (Button, Icon Button, Link, Checkbox, Radio, Switch, Slider, Tag) consumes this primitive rather than defining its own focus treatment.
Use the FocusRing component when wrapping exactly one child is straightforward.
Use the exported focusRingClassNames object directly when a component needs to compose other classes onto the same element (e.g. a custom checkbox's native input).
themeRules: Must be visible with sufficient contrast on both light and dark surfaces via --color-border-focused.
implementationNotes: Use React.memo for the exported component.
No hardcoded colors or widths - use --color-border-focused, --border-width-md.
Exports both a component (FocusRing) and a raw classNames object (focusRingClassNames) as two entry points to the same CSS, not two separate implementations.
do: Wrap the one interactive child that needs a focus indicator.
Use focusRingClassNames when a component must compose its own classes onto the same element.
dont: Do not apply Focus Ring to a non-interactive element to fake a focus state.
Do not write a new :focus-visible rule instead of reusing this primitive.
Do not expect Focus Ring to add keyboard interaction on its own.
acceptanceCriteria: Renders the child with focus classes merged onto its className.
Outline only appears on :focus-visible, in both light and dark themes.
focusRingClassNames exposes focusRing, focusRingDefault, and focusRingDisabled for direct composition.
knownLimitations: The 2px outline offset is not yet backed by a dedicated design token.
Outset ring only - no inset variant.

borderWidth currently accepts only 'default' - Figma removed the 1px/compact option, and no component in the codebase ever consumed it. The prop is kept (rather than removed) in case a future dense-control variant is introduced.
futureEnhancements: A documented per-component radius-inheritance strategy for edge cases where border-radius: inherit isn't sufficient
